sermon.title: Leaders of the Family
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches family leadership: husbands and wives building wisely, ruling the house with honesty, providing for their own (1 Timothy 5:8), and raising children in the nurture of the Lord with real consequences. From Cain and Seth, Noah, and Eli’s failure to restrain his sons, he shows that love disciplines and that the family is the key to church and nation.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: “do unto others” called the second commandment; Cain and Seth marrying sisters and the bully narrative are his own “hillbilly imagination”; “once saved always saved” challenged (doctrinal). Sensitive content kept as spoken: the Quran permitting wife-beating, fathers arranging sexual “coming of age” for children (as examples of commands not “in the Lord”), welfare recipients vs illegal aliens, public schools “forcing homosexual and evolution lies.” A private first name appears only in the transcript.

If one man sins against another, God will judge him. But if a man sins against the LORD, who will intercede for him?” Nevertheless they did not heed the voice of their father, because the LORD desired to kill them.
For I have told him that I will judge his house forever for the iniquity which he knows, because his sons made themselves vile, and he did not restrain them.

Also your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead; and the ark of God has been captured.” Then it happened, when he made mention of the ark of God, that Eli fell off the seat backward by the side of the gate; and his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.

scriptures.text_nkjv: He who spares his rod hates his son, But he who loves him disciplines him promptly.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself for her,

Wives, submit to your own husbands, as to the Lord. For the husband is head of the wife, as also Christ is head of the church; and He is the Savior of the body. Therefore, just as the church is subject to Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in everything. Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself for her, that He might sanctify and cleanse her with the washing of water by the word, that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish. So husbands ought to love their own wives as their own bodies; he who loves his wife loves himself. For no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as the Lord does the church. For we are members of His body, of His flesh and of His bones. “For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.” This is a great mystery, but I speak concerning Christ and the church. Nevertheless let each one of you in particular so love his own wife as himself, and let the wife see that she respects her husband.

faqs.question: Does God recognize a marriage outside a church?
faqs.answer: Yes—once you make the commitment, God recognizes it.

faqs.question: Is every man the head of every woman?
faqs.answer: No—a wife is under her husband, and daughters under their dad.

faqs.question: Does a wife working change God’s order?
What will God ask a husband and father?
faqs.answer: What he did with the responsibility God gave him.

faqs.question: What faith are we supposed to have?
faqs.answer: That Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, so we might have life.

faqs.question: Is discipline without consequence enough?
faqs.answer: No—discipline without a consequence isn’t discipline.

faqs.question: Does God give responsibility without ability?
faqs.answer: No, he says God never does.
